blocks.body: How can nematode chemical signals in soil be converted into useful detection information? Our dry-lab work addresses this question by connecting receptor engineering, dynamic structural analysis, signal and color-development simulations, and economic evaluation, progressively exploring a path from ascaroside recognition to agricultural management.

Together, the four components form a research pathway: Receptor engineering proposes recognition hypotheses; dynamic simulations add structural interpretations; signaling and dual-channel models explore density inference; and the economic model evaluates the value of information. Docking and molecular dynamics (MD) inform sensor design. ODEs, the dual-channel model, and Eco connect through color-development and density interfaces, while the precision needed for management tiers feeds back into subsequent detection calibration.
